notes.decision: The recurring formula on this page is 'X is rooted (ϩⲟⲩⲏⲥ) within him, established (ⲥⲙⲁⲛⲧ) beneath him.' ϩⲟⲩⲏⲥ is most likely a Lycopolitan qualitative of a verb of fixing/setting, paired here in synonymous parallelism with ⲥⲙⲁⲛⲧ ('established'). I render it 'rooted' to capture an organic-fixing sense distinct from the architectural 'established.' ⲛⲏⲧϥ = Lyc for ⲛ̄ϩⲏⲧϥ̄ 'in him'; ⲛⲥⲏⲧϥ = ⲛⲥⲱⲧϥ̄/ⲛ̄ⲥⲱⲧⲡ̄ 'beneath/within him.' The pair encodes Manichaean cosmic foundation: each emanation is rooted within the higher and stably established below it.

ⲡⲧⲭⲁⲓ here = ⲡⲭⲁⲓ̈ 'abode/vessel/body' (per accumulated vocabulary); ⲙⲙⲟⲩⲗⲉⲩⲉ = Greek loan βουλεύω 'deliberate, take counsel,' used substantivally as 'counsels/deliberations.' Translated 'abode of the counsels' rather than 'body of the counsels' to capture the dwelling-sense in the Manichaean schema where the Greatness houses the divine deliberations.

The bare ⲕ̄ⲁ at line 13, again in line 15 (twice), and the ⲛ̄ⲥⲉ at line 16 form the decorative chapter-heading frame around the title at line 14. ⲕ̄ⲁ = Greek alphabetic numeral 21. This identifies the new chapter as Kephalaion 21: 'Concerning the Father of the Greatness, that he is established and fixed [forever].'

Function uncertain. Possible readings: (1) numerical/scribal mark closing the heading frame; (2) Lycopolitan ⲛ̄ⲥⲏ ('thus, so be it'); (3) a corrupt or abbreviated form. The line is otherwise blank, supporting a structural-frame interpretation. Left in Coptic with English placeholder.
Standard kephalaion-opening formula 'Once again the Apostle said' — with ⲡⲁⲭⲉ = ⲡⲉϫⲁϥ 'he said' (per accumulated vocabulary). The Apostle here = Mani.

ⲛⲁⲥⲣⲛ̄ analyzed as future ⲛⲁ- + verbal stem ⲥⲣⲛ̄, most plausibly Lyc reflex of ⲥⲱⲣ 'spread, scatter, pour out' (qualitative/causative). Translated 'shall be poured out upon' to fit the soteriological context: the light of the Father shall come upon those who hear and shall lead them to recognize him.

Conjunctive 3pl 'and they shall recognize-him,' with ⲥⲛⲟⲩⲱⲛ = ⲥⲟⲩⲛ̄ⲟⲩⲱⲛ 'recognize/discern' (per accumulated vocabulary), continuing across the line break to ⲛⲉϩ at the start of line 20 (= 3sg.m. object pronoun).

ⲡϣⲁⲣⲓⲧ = Lyc reflex of ϣⲟⲣⲡ 'first.' Therefore 'the First Father of the Greatness' = the Father of Greatness as primal-source emanation, distinguished from the subsequent five Greatnesses he generates.
ⲡϥⲧ = Lycopolitan reduction of ⲡⲉϥϯⲟⲩ 'his five.' Confirmed by the immediately following enumeration in line 23 of the canonical five faculties (ⲛⲟⲩⲥ, ⲙⲉⲩⲉ, ⲥⲃⲱ, ⲥⲁⲭⲛⲉ, ⲙⲁⲕⲙⲉⲕ). Not 'four members.'

notes.decision: The canonical five intellectual faculties of the Father (also of the soul). Translated per the mandatory terminology: mind / thought / teaching / counsel / reflection. ⲧⲥⲃⲱ = 'teaching' (NOT 'insight').

From qualitative ⲥⲙⲁⲙⲁⲁⲧ 'blessed' substantivized = 'the Blessed One' — likely a divine epithet of the Father here, the source of the gushing-forth of the great members of light. ⲃⲉⲃⲉ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ = 'gushed forth' per accumulated vocabulary (cosmogonic verb).
Adverbial phrase from ⲟⲩⲱⲧ 'single, alone' = 'in oneness / uniquely / as a unity.' Describes the mode in which the great members emanate from the Father — single in source, multiple in expression.

= ⲥϯⲛⲟⲩϥⲉ 'sweet smell, fragrance.' In the correspondential register, the second of the five great members of light IS a fragrance — direct sensory-correspondence (cf. ⲧⲏⲥⲧⲉ 'scent' in earlier vocabulary).

ⲥⲣⲁⲩ = Lycopolitan ⲥⲣⲁⲩ/ⲍⲣⲁⲩ = ϩⲣⲟⲟⲩ 'voice' (in vocabulary). Third of the great members IS his beautiful voice. The five members thus form a sensory-cosmological correspondence series: light, fragrance, voice, [fourth — perhaps touch or word], [fifth].
